highlights.title: OpenAI to End Partnership With Cursor After SpaceX Acquisition
highlights.description: OpenAI said it will end its partnership with Cursor after the AI-coding agent’s acquisition by SpaceX, according to a post on X.

highlights.title: Meta’s $18 billion settlement puts TikTok and YouTube on notice. Who's next on the firing line?
highlights.description: "Meta is seeking to ensure its competitors will face the same rules," one business professor told CNBC after Meta called on rivals to protect children online.

highlights.title: Ripple is preparing XRP Ledger for quantum computers before ‘Q-Day’ arrives
highlights.description: An Anthropic model cut the work needed to break a leading post-quantum signature candidate by a factor of 67 million last month, while Bitcoin and Ethereum published their own migration plans this week.

highlights.title: Microsoft-backed AI data center faces backlash over 62 unpermitted gas turbines and 1.5M-gallon LNG tank — issues with $19.4B facility range from illegal construction to noise pollution
highlights.description: The community surrounding the DataOne data center in Vineland, New Jersey, are complaining about the Microsoft-linked project. The company's deployment of several unpermitted gas turbines is just one of the issues that has been hounding the project, with potential water issues also surfacing in recent weeks.

highlights.title: Tech backlash reaches fever pitch as AI angst collides with social media fears
highlights.description: With data center concerns becoming a major election issue and Meta reaching a landmark settlement in a social media case, the tech backlash is gaining steam.

highlights.title: Chinese Chipmaker CXMT Sues Pentagon to Get Off US Blacklist
highlights.description: CXMT Corp. filed a lawsuit against the US Department of Defense, seeking removal from a blacklist that identified the Chinese chipmaker as a supporter of the Communist country’s military.
